metadata.case_name: CHOW SHUK YAN v. THE SECRETARY FOR JUSTICE

plaintiff.occupation_before: Student (Associate Degree of Music at the Hong Kong Institute of Education) and part-time lifeguard with the Leisure and Cultural Services Department
plaintiff.occupation_after: Music teacher / private piano teacher; assistant music teacher (worked at Melocity Music Learning Centre and Grace Piano Company); ad hoc music classes

injuries.description: Post-Concussion Syndrome (PCS) with headache and dizziness related to the accident.
source: The medical report dated 21 August 200X of Dr Po Yin-Chung of PMH Neurosurgery Department stated the Plaintiff had Post-Concussion Syndrome (PCS) with headache and dizziness related to the accident.
Ever since discharge, the Plaintiff complained of persistent tinnitus, headache, dizziness and convulsions (in issue as to when first set in), and she had to go to hospital from time to time.
The medical report dated 21 March 2005 of Dr Ng Tat-Yuen, the Plaintiff’s ENT expert, stated that tinnitus will likely to be permanent, and will limit the full potential as a music teacher.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of middle or inner ear

source: On the next day, she was admitted to Yan Chai Hospital with persistent vertigo (dizziness) with suspected Hyper-Ventilation Syndrome (HVS).
HVS means breathing too heavily, leading to excessive inhalation of oxygen and depletion of carbon dioxide in the body, associated with muscular spasms, bodily cramps and convulsions.
Diagnosis was Otitis Media (middle ear infection).
injuries.icd_description: Injury of middle or inner ear

injuries.description: Mild atrophy (wasting) of the brain on CT scan
source: CT scan showed no brain haemorrhage but mild atrophy (wasting).

manifestations.description: impaired mental functions (memory and speech slurring)

treatments_received: A&E attendance and admission to Princess Margaret Hospital
Chinese medicine treatment (Mainland and Baptist Hospital)
Neurology consultations with Dr Brian Choa
Admission to Yan Chai Hospital (2 days) and other short hospital admissions
treatments_future: psychotherapeutic sessions (8 to 12) for relaxation and breathing techniques
neurological treatment on an "as and when necessary" basis

losses.description: Limitation on full potential as a music teacher / loss of opportunity to advance music career and pursue certain music industry paths; claimed loss of congenial employment as a piano performer and impact on teaching career.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Unable to continue swimming and lifeguard work; near drowning episode led to giving up swimming.
